body.p: I. Status of the Claims

By this Reply, Applicant amends claims 1, 9, and 17. Since the amendment filed November 16, 2020, was not entered (see Advisory Action at Section 3(a)), claim amendments are made relative to the claims filed July 14, 2020. The originally filed specification, e.g., paragraph [0046], and drawings fully support the subject matter of the amended and new claims. No new matter has been added. II. Interview
Applicant thanks Examiner Alter for the courtesies extended during the

telephonic interview of December 1, 2020. The remarks provided in the Advisory Action and the examiner Initiated Interview Summary, both dated December 8, 2020, are consistent with the issues discussed during the interview. III. Section 112(b) Rejections

In the Office Action, claims 1-20 were rejected as allegedly indefinite under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) based on the use of the phrase "a healthy or average blood flow characteristic" recited in each of claims 1, 9, and 17. (Office Action at p.2.) While Applicant does not agree that this phrase renders the claims unclear, to further prosecution, Applicant has amended each of independent claims 1, 9, and 17 to recite, "a predetermined healthy or average blood flow characteristic based on a population- based measurement or estimate." Support for this feature can be found at least at paragraph [0046] of the specification as filed.
This phrase in each of independent claims 1, 9, and 17 is clear and definite. For example, the characteristic of the claims is "based on a population-based measurement

or estimate." While this feature may be broad since different populations may be used to determine the measurement or estimate, the breadth of the claim should not be confused with indefiniteness. MPEP 2173.04. Accordingly, withdrawal of the Section 112(b) rejections is respectfully submitted. IV. Section 103 Rejections

In the Office Action, claims 1-20 which were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over one or more of Taylor (U.S. Publication No. 2012/0041318 A1), Mabotuwana et al. ("A model of blood flow in the mesenteric arterial system" Biomed Eng Onlin. 2007), Walker ("Mesenteric vasculature and collateral pathways" Seminars in interventional radiology vol. 26, 3 (2009): 167-74), Taub et al. (U.S. Publication No. 2012/0088955), and/or Heldt et al. ("Scaling cardiovascular parameters for population simulations." Computers in Cardiology, 2004. IEEE).

Claim 1 recites, in part, "determining a threshold blood flow characteristic based on the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's bowel, the threshold blood flow characteristic comprising a healthy or average blood flow characteristic based on a population-based measurement or estimate." In rejecting claim 1, the Office Action contends that Taylor teaches "a range or threshold of intensity values centered at the selected intensity value." (Office Action at p. 7.) And while the Office Action acknowledges that Taylor fails to teach "determining a threshold blood flow characteristic," the Office Action contends that Taub at Heldt teach this feature and, thus, cure the deficiency of Taylor. (Id. at p. 11.)
Taylor discloses a threshold value for intensity values of an image. (Taylor at para. [0135].) Taub discloses determining a threshold suction flow rate based on fluid

flowing through a device 200. (Para. [0230].) The Office Action asserts that Heldt discloses setting parameters, generating steady-state values, and compare to the model's prediction. (Office Action at p. 11.) None of these references, however, discloses determining a threshold based on the patient-specific model, and having the threshold including characteristics associated with a healthy population. Put another way, none of the references determine a threshold using both characteristics associated with a healthy population and the patient-specific model.
The Examiner Initiated Interview Summary dated December 8, 2020,

acknowledges that none of the applied art teaches "determining a threshold blood flow characteristic based on the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's bowel, the threshold blood flow characteristic comprising a healthy or average blood flow characteristic based on a population-based measurement or estimate," but asserts that it would have been obvious to arrive at this claim limitation. (Examiner Initiated Interview Summary at p. 3.) The Interview Summary does not provide evidence for this conclusion. The Interview Summary quotes a passage in the Introduction from Heldt. (Id.) But this passage merely states that a model can be used to predict hemodynamic conditions, and that data can be compared to hemodynamic data from healthy individuals. (Id.) As set forth above, none of the applied art, including Heldt, determines a threshold based on the patient-specific model, and having the threshold including characteristics associated with a healthy population as recited in independent claim 1.

For at least the foregoing reasons, independent claim 1 and claims dependent therefrom are patentably distinguishable over the applied art. While of different scope, independent claims 9 and 17 recite similarly distinguishing features as discussed above
relative to independent claim 1. Thus, independent claims 9 and 17, and claims dependent therefrom, are patentably distinguishable over the applied art at least for the foregoing reasons.
V. Conclusion

The Office Action and the Advisory Action contain characterizations of the claims and the related art with which the applicant does not necessarily agree. Unless expressly noted otherwise, applicant declines to subscribe to any statement or characterization in the Office Action or the Advisory Action.
In discussing the specification, claims, and drawings in this Reply, it is to be

understood that Applicant is in no way intending to limit the scope of the claims to any exemplary embodiments described in the specification or abstract and/or shown in the drawings. Rather, Applicant is entitled to have the claims interpreted broadly to the maximum extent permitted by statute, regulation, and applicable case law.

In view of the foregoing remarks, Applicant submits that this claimed invention is neither anticipated nor rendered obvious in view of the prior art references cited against this application. Applicant therefore requests the reconsideration and reexamination of the application, and the timely allowance of the pending claims.
